newsitem.title: USA: Latin American firms favor Compaq over IBM - survey.
newsitem.headline: Latin American firms favor Compaq over IBM - survey.

text.p: Executives buying information technology equipment for top Latin American corporations favour Compaq Computer Corp. personal computers over IBM's by a margin of three to two, a survey released Thursday shows.
Compaq was the top vendor for more than 25 percent of 722 large companies throughout Latin America by consultants International Data Corp.

About 15 percent favoured International Business Machines Corp. machines, slightly more than those who preferred personal computers built by Acer Inc. and Hewlett-Packard Co., International Data Vice President Paul Pastrone told a technology marketing conference here. Machines made by Digital Equipment Corp. and Dell Computer Corp. were chosen as the favourite by fewer executives than those picking local brands.

Pastrone said the findings could be a boon for Compaq, since many leading Latin American companies are rethinking the practice of buying many different brands and considering purchasing all personal computers from a single vendor.

Although accounting for only 3 percent of worldwide information technology expenditures, Latin America last year showed a 20.9 percent spending increase over 1995 while the worldwide sector growth rate was 13.1 percent in 1996.
